B01017.caption: The four phases of a round in order. If a specific rule places the Monster Phase before the Party Phase, both phases still resolve once before End of Round (see 3.1).

B01074.caption: Left: the activation procedure. Right: a Hero's 3 AP across one round, assuming a shield: Move (1 AP) and Attack (1 AP) leave 1 AP, which a Block Reaction (1 AP) uses in the Monster Phase; otherwise it is removed at End of Round (see 3.3).

B01530.caption: The five-step attack sequence and the Mitigation Order. Source example: 6 slashing and 4 fire damage against 5 AV is (6 - 5) + 4 = 5 damage; with d6 AD rolling 3, 9 slashing is 9 - 3 = 6, or 9 - (3 + 2) = 4 with a +2 AV Block (see 5.2).

B00600.caption: Tabletop Mode measures between closest points; Grid Mode counts orthogonal squares as 1" and diagonal squares as 1.5", so this range is 1.5 + 1.5 + 1 = 4" without the source square. Footprints follow Sz, and movement is declared and verified before it is resolved (see 2.6).

B01333.caption: Source example: a Speed 5" Move of 1 + 1.5 + 1.5 = 4" leaves 1", enough for one orthogonal square but not for another 1.5" diagonal. Difficult Terrain costs 2" orthogonal and 3" diagonal, a multi-square footprint pays the highest cost among its squares, and a diagonal step needs an open orthogonal route (see 4.4.3).

B01481.caption: Adjacency to an enemy that is not Knocked Out causes Engagement; a Knocked Out combatant is never Engaged. Reach extends melee attacks without changing Engagement. Move out of melee distance may trigger Reflex Attack; Shift and forced movement do not (see 5.1 and 5.5.4).

B00812.caption: Blocking Terrain, a corner shared by two Blocking squares and the interior of Cover Terrain block LOS. Touching only a Cover Terrain corner, an intervening combatant and Impassable Terrain leave LOS clear and give the target Cover (Impassable Terrain unless its terrain entry says otherwise); an orthogonal 1" Shift [1 AP] clear of the line removes that Cover (see 2.7.2 and 2.8.4).

B00743.caption: A Grid Mode Aura 2" from a single source square affects 13 squares (including the source square); a 3" Cone affects 7 squares beyond its origin square, and does not affect the combatant it originates from unless a rule says otherwise. A square whose sight line from the origin is blocked by Blocking Terrain is unaffected even if the template covers it, and shared area damage is rolled once (see 2.7.3).

B01377.caption: Forced movement follows a line and stops at the last legal position; a Collision deals no damage by itself. Source example: a 3" Push toward a ledge 2" away moves the Skeleton 2" to the edge point, then Falling is resolved from that point (see 4.4.6).

B07627.caption: A Monster Group begins Resting and becomes Awake for the rest of the adventure when a trigger occurs: an enemy moving within 6" (no LOS needed), a visible enemy entering LOS within 12", damage, a loud event within 6", or a scenario rule (see 9.4).

B07673.caption: The Standard Monster AI Script: a Monster executes the first valid instruction and its activation then ends unless a rule explicitly says it continues. Each instruction is tried only if the one above it does not apply (see 9.5 C).

B07701.caption: Primary Target is the nearest visible enemy; equal candidates are separated by lowest current HP, then Most Recent Attacker, then Random Determination. If the Monster cannot reach a position from which it may attack its Primary Target this activation, but can reach such a position against another visible enemy, the nearest such enemy becomes the new Primary Target (see 9.5 E and 9.5 F).

B11101.caption: Deployment patterns used by the Core Scenarios, drawn on a 36"×36" battlefield: opposite long or short edges within 6", a Setup Roll-off winner's choice of edge or 8"×8" corner, and opposite corner zones with alternating placement. Where a scenario is silent, the 10.1 step 7 default supplies the 6" depth and 8"×8" corner size; step 11 supplies the placing order; key: FIG-20 (see 10.1 and each scenario's Party Deployment).

Special deployments: a Trail with at least two Heroes on it (or the party's only Hero), one shared short edge within 8" (no Hero within 6" of an opposing Hero), a central 8"×8" Safe Zone (no Hero within 3" of an opposing Hero), and short edges either side of a Ravine; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4).
Template, not a fixed battlefield: twelve Preparation Steps, step 7 default zones and terrain restrictions, and step 11 deployment; key: FIG-20 (see 10.1).

B13040.caption: In The Chasm Crossing the Survey Map starts 3" from the first ledge and must be placed adjacent to the Cartographer's Stone 3" beyond the last ledge. A failed Jump leaves the jumper Prone before the gap; forced movement into the Chasm or a failed Crumbling Ledge Check causes a Chasm Fall, with the stated Fly or Climb exceptions; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4).

B12143.caption: In the Whispering Grove the Antlered Warden is placed adjacent to the first Standing Stone a Hero Interacts with, and its Target Priority is the valid Hero who most recently activated or attempted to activate a Stone, whichever party that Hero belongs to. Entangling Roots then applies if the target is within 8"; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4).

B15246.caption: Each adventure runs Expedition, Skirmish, Aftermath, then Town; Aftermath and Town follow every adventure, win or lose, unless a rule says otherwise. The Town Phase grants 4 TAP, or the Journey-modified amount, to spend at six locations (see 11.2).

B16422.caption: Appendix A starting positions, with the Dispatch Satchel adjacent to the centre ruin, and Round 1 of the sample game. Edric ends the round with 16 - 5 = 11, 11 - 3 = 8 and 8 - 3 = 5 HP after Varek's attack and two Dire Wolf bites; key: FIG-20 (see A.11).

B17653.caption: Basic Mode setup for The Courier's Strongbox on a 24"×24" battlefield, with one complete Monster group per Entry marker, assigned at random. Assumed example: carrying the Strongbox cuts Ironscar's SPD 4" by 2" to 2" per Move; extracting it with 1 Satchel, having defeated 2 Goblins and 1 Bandit, scores 12 + 4 + 2 + 3 = 21c; key: FIG-20 (see B.6).

B12013.caption: Key to the setup and deployment diagrams: symbols for Heroes, zones, markers, Monster Groups, terrain, distances and edges, with the orientation, scale and grey-dashed conventions every such diagram follows (see 10.4).

B12068.caption: Hunt the Wild Beast: parties deploy within 6" of opposite long battlefield edges, and the Great Forest Boar starts within 2" of the Mud Wallow near the centre; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Greenmark Scenario 1).

B12139.caption: The Whispering Grove: parties deploy in opposite 8"×8" corners; three Standing Stones stand 6–8" apart in a Central Clearing about 12–15" across; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Greenmark Scenario 2).

B12213.caption: The Bandit's Toll: parties deploy within 6" of the opposite short edges where a Trail 3–4" wide runs, with at least two Heroes, or the only Hero, of each party on the Trail; the Barricade and Wagon 2 stand at the midpoint; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Greenmark Scenario 3).

B12281.caption: The Spider's Silk Route: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges on higher ground, either side of a Ravine 6–8" wide that cuts across the midpoint with the first Silk Bundle in the central Webbed Section and two others at least 4" away; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Greenmark Scenario 4).

B12357.caption: The Ambushed Emissary: parties deploy in opposite 8"×8" corners; the Bandit Camp lies in one quadrant at least 8" from every edge, with four Clue markers at least 6" from each other and the Camp; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Greenmark Scenario 5).

B12441.caption: Ritual of the Old Growth: the Setup Roll-off winner picks a long edge and deploys within 6"; the Mother Tree at the centre has a Sacred Grove within 6" of it, with three Treasure Chests evenly spaced on its outer edge; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Greenmark Scenario 6).

B12524.caption: The Fallen Observatory: parties deploy within 6" of opposite long edges around a central 6"×6" Collapsed Dome holding the Star Lens, with two raised Platforms at least 10" apart; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Ashlands Scenario 1).

B12589.caption: The Guardian's Test: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges, with the Sealed Gateway in one long edge and three Trial Pedestals at least 5" apart in a Courtyard about 15"×15"; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Ashlands Scenario 2).

B12647.caption: The Shifting Sands of Time: parties deploy in opposite 8"×8" corners around a 4"×4" Central Ruin with four 3"×3" Unstable Ground zones at least 6" apart; carriers escape by the two edges not touching their corner; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Ashlands Scenario 3).

B12723.caption: The Sealed Archive: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges around an 8"×4" Archive Hall with the Codex on its lectern, two side chambers and Tablet Caches two in one chamber and one in the other; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Ashlands Scenario 4).

B12802.caption: The Reliquary of Broken Saints: parties deploy within 6" of opposite long edges around a long central nave with the Reliquary on its altar platform, Bone Fragments in the two side aisles; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Ashlands Scenario 5).

B12889.caption: The Iron-Vein Vault: parties deploy within 6" of opposite long edges around a central 6"×6" Chamber with an iron door whose hinges and lock carry the Binding Points, and the Vault Record 3" beyond the door; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Ashlands Scenario 6).

B12972.caption: The Crystal Harvest: parties deploy in opposite 8"×8" corners; two Main Caverns 8"×8" are linked by narrow passages, with a central Crystal Node midway between them; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Undermarches Scenario 1).

B13038.caption: The Chasm Crossing: both parties deploy within 8" of one short edge, no Heroes within 6" of an opposing Hero; the Chasm 8" wide bisects the battlefield, with the Survey Map and the Stone each 3" from the end ledges; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Undermarches Scenario 2).

B13105.caption: The Quake: both parties deploy inside a central 8"×8" Safe Zone, no Hero within 3" of an opposing Hero; the Setup Roll-off winner designates the Main Exit and the two perpendicular edges are Collapsed Tunnels; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Undermarches Scenario 3).

B13208.caption: The Undermarches Outpost Raid: parties deploy in opposite 8"×8" corners around an outpost with a central 3"×3" Command Tent holding the Battle Plans and 2–3 Guard Towers; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Undermarches Scenario 4).

B13281.caption: The Shadowed Under Passage: Party A deploys within 6" of the short edge farther from the Heart, Party B within 6" of the opposite edge; a winding Under Passage runs between the two edges and the Heart lies at least 12" from Party A's edge; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Undermarches Scenario 5).

B13360.caption: The Ritual of Shadow Binding: Party A deploys within 6" of one short edge and Party B within 6" of the opposite one; three Shadow Orbs stand within 2" of the 4" Binding Circle at the centre of the central cavern; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Undermarches Scenario 6).

B13446.caption: Plunder of the Frozen Ruins: parties deploy in opposite 8"×8" corners; the five Chests are placed alternately at least 6" apart and at least 8" from any deployment zone; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Pale City Scenario 1).

B13512.caption: The Alchemist's Frozen Laboratory: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges; the Laboratory, about 6"×8", holds three Reagent Chests and the Alchemical Golem; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Pale City Scenario 2).

B13583.caption: The Haunted Mausoleum: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges outside the mausoleum, which holds a Grand Hall, 3 Burial Crypts and exactly five Sarcophagi; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Pale City Scenario 3).

B13645.caption: The Clockwork Menagerie: the Setup Roll-off winner picks any battlefield edge and deploys within 6"; three Clockwork Guardians start Awake beside the Workbenches or within 3" of the centre; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Pale City Scenario 4).

B13713.caption: The Ice Wyrm's Hoard: parties deploy within 6" of opposite edges where the frozen tunnels enter a central lair about 12"×12", with the Ice Wyrm at its centre and the Hoard within 2" of it; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Pale City Scenario 5).

B13787.caption: The Icebound Court: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges around a central throne chamber where the Frost Bailiff Magistrate begins on the Ice Throne with Ice Mephit Bodyguards within 2"; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Pale City Scenario 6).

B13861.caption: The Oasis Raiders: parties deploy within 6" of opposite long edges around a central Oasis about 8"×8" with the Wellspring, the Raider Chieftain starting within 2" of it; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Sun-Drowned Scenario 1).

B13926.caption: The Cinder Lord's Lost Brazier: parties deploy on opposite short edges converging on a plaza whose 2"×2" Altar has three Elemental Locus pillars 4–6" from it; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Sun-Drowned Scenario 2).

B13997.caption: Tomb of the Sunken Kings: parties deploy in opposite corner zones (8"×8" by the 10.1 default) breaching a tomb complex with a Grand Hall about 5"×10" and three Royal Sarcophagi in separate chambers; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Sun-Drowned Scenario 3).

B14060.caption: The Sandwyrm's Lair: parties deploy within 6" of opposite battlefield edges around a broad sand basin with a central Shifting Sands Zone where the burrowed Sandwyrm first appears; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Sun-Drowned Scenario 4).

B14133.caption: The Cursed Colossus of the Waste: parties deploy within 6" of opposite battlefield edges around a large central Colossus of Blocking Terrain bearing the Glowing Rune and holding the Heartstone; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Sun-Drowned Scenario 5).

B14212.caption: The Cinder Lord's Obsidian Prison: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges around a central Obsidian Dais with three Glyphic Stones evenly arranged around it; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, Sun-Drowned Scenario 6).

B14298.caption: The Reliquary of Edrava Salttide: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges on the driest banks around a central Sunken Barrow whose flooded sanctum holds the Reliquary; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, The Mire Scenario 1).

B14369.caption: The Lizardfolk's Stolen Offerings: parties deploy within 6" of opposite battlefield edges around a swamp encampment where three Offering Piles are placed alternately; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, The Mire Scenario 2).

B14446.caption: The Mire Titan's Fen: parties deploy in opposite corner zones on the outer banks (8"×8" by the 10.1 default), around a central Bubbling Fen where the Mire Titan starts Awake; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, The Mire Scenario 3).

B14521.caption: The Blighted Heartwood: parties deploy within 6" of opposite short edges around a central Blighted Grove about 8"×8" of Thorny Vines with the Heartwood at its centre; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, The Mire Scenario 4).

B14598.caption: Salttide's Reckoning: parties deploy along the outer banks within 6" of opposite long edges (10.1 default) around a central Ritual Island holding Edrava Salttide and three Cursed Effigies; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, The Mire Scenario 5).

B14677.caption: The Serpent's Sunken Hoard: parties deploy outside the Sinkhole area within 6" of opposite short edges (6" is the 10.1 default), around a central Deep Water Sinkhole Pool 10–12" across holding three Hoard Chests; key: FIG-20 (see 10.4, The Mire Scenario 6).

B00405.caption: What you need to play: 1–8 players, a 36"×36" battlefield in Tabletop Mode or Grid Mode, a model for every combatant, markers, record sheets, tracking tokens, and at least 4d4, 4d6, 4d8, 4d10, 2d12, and 2d20 (see 1.4).

B00427.caption: An adventure is a single game: complete the scenario's objective and satisfy its victory conditions, often by comparing secured wealth in coins (Xc). In campaign play the goal is Triumph, and every Hero eventually meets one of three Fates: Die, Retire, or Triumph (see 1.5).

B00435.caption: When two rules conflict, use the more specific rule; if they are equally specific, use the more restrictive rule. Examples, summaries, and reference tables never override the main rules text (see 1.6).

B00508.caption: Heroes and Hirelings use the four ability scores (STR, DEX, INT, and SPI), which may be negative and have no maximum unless a rule says otherwise; Monsters never have or use them. A non-Monster combatant's omitted score counts as +0 for that Check only (see 2.2).

B00525.caption: A Check is 1d20 plus the listed ability score: 12 or higher succeeds and 11 or lower fails, but a natural 1 always fails and a natural 20 always succeeds. In the example, with an assumed +2, Advantage keeps the higher of two d20 and Disadvantage the lower; Monsters never make a Check, except that they automatically succeed on Terrain Checks (see 2.3 and 2.4).

B00822.caption: Concealment climbs from Exposed to Cover to Hidden, and a combatant who loses Cover falls to Exposed. A Light Source creates Light in its Aura (3" unless a rule lists another size), Darkness gives Cover against nonadjacent enemies, and Hidden and Invisible are separate conditions (see 2.8).

B00981.caption: A Hero may spend 1 Luck Point after seeing a d20 Check made by or against that Hero, or a damage roll from or directly affecting that Hero, but before consequences are applied. The entire roll is rerolled once and the new result must be used; if several Heroes could spend Luck, the side that won Initiative decides first (see 2.10).

B01037.caption: Competitive Initiative in order, with whose modifier is used, the three tie-breakers, and the solo and cooperative pointer. Source example: the Road Wardens roll 17 to the opposing side's 14, win Initiative, and choose to act second (see 3.2).

B01130.caption: The End of Round resolves in four steps once both the Party Phase and Monster Phase have resolved. In the assumed example, 2 damage at step 1 reduces 4 Temporary HP to 2, step 2 removes the rest, and step 3 removes 1 unspent AP (see 3.5).

B01156.caption: The five timing terms placed along a round, and the order for effects that resolve at the same time when no rule is more specific. Solo and cooperative play replace the first two steps with the round's phase order (see 3.6).

B01449.caption: A Reaction to an attack or damaging effect is declared before any of its source's damage dice are rolled, and each affected combatant has only 1 Reaction that modifies the same action or effect. A Reaction that depends on the roll commits its costs in advance and releases them if its trigger does not occur (see 4.5).

B01463.caption: Targets must be legal when an action is declared and when it resolves. An action that becomes illegal before it resolves fails and its AP remains spent, unless it was abandoned during Declared State verification (see 4.6).

B01741.caption: Push moves a target 2" directly away on a successful STR Check with Disadvantage; Trip makes a target of your Sz or smaller Prone on a successful STR or DEX Check with Disadvantage. Neither is an attack, and neither counts toward the multi-attack Disadvantage chain (see 5.6).

B01762.caption: The second and each later counted weapon attack a Hero or Hireling makes in one activation rolls its base damage dice with Disadvantage unless a rule says otherwise. Push, Trip, attacks granted by a Reaction, and a Riposte do not count toward the chain (see 5.7).

B02049.caption: The ten steps of Hero creation in order, with the formulas for final ability scores and starting Max HP. After each base value is calculated, every applicable ancestry, background, class, Talent, item, and random-generation modifier applies (see 6.2).

B02096.caption: What every Hero records, the derived Initiative Bonus and Base Max NRG, and how current values follow their maximums. In the example, Max HP falling to 6 reduces current HP from 7 to 6, and raising Max HP back to 10 does not restore it (see 6.4).

B03244.caption: APL adds the Levels of the Heroes in the Active Party, divides by their number, and rounds down; Hirelings, Summons, and Heroes on the Bench do not count. Example: Levels 3, 3, 2, and 2 give 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, so APL 2 (see 6.14).

B03329.caption: The matched one-off party rules: one Hero Level from 1–10 for every Hero, Gaining a Level resolved once per Level above 1 without Training Costs, coins pooled and spent at list price before deployment, and the limits that apply to both sides. Example: a chosen Level 4 means 4 - 1 = 3 resolutions (see 6.17).

B03413.caption: Two real entries split into the six elements 7.3 lists in order: Shovel (7.16) uses five and Spidermilk Venom (7.14) uses two, since an entry omits any element that does not apply. Other item tables use other fields (see 7.3).

B03417.caption: The eight stacking and precedence rules of 7.4: what stacks, how damage type and damage order resolve, how a target restriction overrides Hidden, Invisible, LOS, and adjacency, and how illegal spaces and duplicated Reactions are handled. The example uses assumed item bonuses of +1 and +2 and item penalties of -1 and -3 (see 7.4).
